bib.title: Recursive Deep Models for Semantic Compositionality Over a Sentiment Treebank

read.skipped: Supplementary material (dataset collection details) is referenced but not in the PDF.

question: Can a richer phrase-level sentiment resource plus a tensor-based recursive composition function capture compositional sentiment effects such as negation better than bag-of-words and earlier recursive models?
hypothesis: A single, more powerful multiplicative (tensor) composition function with a fixed number of parameters composes meaning more accurately than many input-specific ones (MV-RNN) or a plain RNN.
contributions: Stanford Sentiment Treebank: fine-grained sentiment labels for 215,154 phrases in parse trees of 11,855 sentences
Analyses of negation, contrastive conjunction and most positive/negative phrases

method.summary: Movie-review sentences from Pang and Lee were parsed, every phrase was labeled by Mechanical Turk workers on a slider, and recursive neural models (RNN, MV-RNN, RNTN) were trained with a softmax at every tree node. Hyperparameters were cross-validated on the dev set.
method.task: Sentiment classification (5-class fine-grained and binary) at every node of a parse tree

datasets.name: Stanford Sentiment Treebank
datasets.size: 11,855 sentences, 215,154 phrases, each annotated by 3 human judges
datasets.split: train 8544 / dev 1101 / test 2210 sentences; positive/negative-only: 6920/872/1821 sentences (neutral filtered, about 20% of data)
datasets.source: Pang and Lee (2005) rottentomatoes.com excerpts (10,662 sentences, half positive, half negative); parsed with Stanford parser; labelled on Amazon Mechanical Turk
datasets.preprocessing: Lowercased text mapped back to original capitalized text; leftover HTML tags and non-English sentences deleted; parser splits about 1,100 snippets into multiple sentences; 25-value slider merged into 5 classes

models.name: RNTN
models.architecture: Recursive tensor network, p=f([b;c]^T V[1:d] [b;c] + W[b;c]), shared across nodes, softmax per node, f=tanh
models.hidden: inferred: word vector size d between 25 and 35 (best range for all models)
models.context: variable-length phrase via binary parse tree

other.tensor: V in R^{2d x 2d x d}

models.name: RNN
models.architecture: p=tanh(W[b;c]), W in R^{d x 2d}; no reconstruction loss

models.name: MV-RNN
models.params: orders of magnitude more parameters than other models (not stated numerically)
models.architecture: vector and matrix per word; matrices initialized as d x d identity plus Gaussian noise

models.name: NB, SVM, BiNB, VecAvg
models.architecture: bag of words NB; SVM; bag of bigrams NB; average of neural word vectors

training.objective: Cross-entropy summed over all tree nodes plus L2 penalty lambda*||theta||^2, theta=(V,W,Ws,L)
training.regularisation: L2 weight regularization, strength cross-validated (value not stated)
training.wall_clock: converges in less than 3 hours to a local optimum; best dev performance usually after 3 - 5 hours

other.tuning: dev set cross-validation over regularization, word vector size, learning rate, minibatch size
other.nonlinearity: no nonlinearity dropped accuracy by over 5%; tanh used in all experiments

inference.decoding: argmax of softmax at each node

metrics.name: Accuracy (5-class fine-grained, all nodes and root)
metrics.definition: fraction of nodes (or sentence roots) with correct class

metrics.name: Accuracy (binary positive/negative, all nodes and root)
metrics.definition: as above with neutral sentences removed

metrics.name: Negation reversal accuracy
metrics.definition: Negated positive: correct sentiment inversion; negated negative: increase in positive activation

metrics.name: X but Y accuracy
metrics.definition: correct only if X, Y and the lowest node dominating 'but' and Y all have correct sentiment (strict, X and Y differ)

eval.protocol: Single test split; no seeds, runs or significance tests stated.

availability.code: http://nlp.stanford.edu/sentiment (training and testing code, live demo)

limits: Models are trained and tested on one corpus (movie review sentences) with one split; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported.
Needs parse trees and phrase-level labels; negation test sets are tiny (21 positive sentences, 131 X-but-Y cases).
Learning rate, regularization value and exact parameter counts are not stated; dataset collection details are in unseen supplementary material.
Fine-grained root accuracy remains under 46%; neutral class is hard.
Dated: recursive parse-tree models have been superseded by sequence and transformer models; SST remains an evaluation set.
